arabic.text: وَكَوَاعِبَ أَتْرَابًۭا (٣٣) وَكَأْسًۭا دِهَاقًۭا (٣٤) لَّا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْوًۭا وَلَا كِذَّٰبًۭا (٣٥) جَزَآءًۭ مِّن رَّبِّكَ عَطَآءً حِسَابًۭا (٣٦) رَّبِّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ۖ لَا يَمْلِكُونَ مِنْهُ خِطَابًۭا (٣٧)

يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلرُّوحُ وَٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ صَفًّۭا ۖ لَّا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ وَقَالَ صَوَابًۭا (٣٨) ذَٰلِكَ ٱلْيَوْمُ ٱلْحَقُّ ۖ فَمَن شَآءَ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ مَـَٔابًا (٣٩) إِنَّآ أَنذَرْنَٰكُمْ عَذَابًۭا قَرِيبًۭا يَوْمَ يَنظُرُ ٱلْمَرْءُ مَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ وَيَقُولُ ٱلْكَافِرُ يَٰلَيْتَنِى كُنتُ تُرَٰبًۢا (٤٠)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: No ill speech will they hear therein or any falsehood -
[As] reward from your Lord, [a generous] gift [made due by] account,
[From] the Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Merciful. They possess not from Him [authority for] speech.
The Day that the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows, they will not speak except for one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he will say what is correct.
That is the True Day; so he who wills may take to his Lord a [way of] return.
Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment on the Day when a man will observe what his hands have put forth and the disbeliever will say, "Oh, I wish that I were dust!"

head: Word
Where
Rule
How to read it
rows: Idgham with ghunnah; then idgham without ghunnah (noon into ر)
Ikhfa': noon before ش; madd muttasil

questions.q: Chunk and link An-Naba' 78:33-40 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 78:33-40 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 78:33-40 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Recite all of An-Naba' to a partner.
78:39 says 'whoever wills may take to his Lord a way of return'. What does that teach about choice?
questions.a: Allah has made the way clear; each person is responsible for choosing it.

questions.q: Who may speak on that Day (78:38)?
options: Only one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he says what is right
questions.a: A) Only one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he says what is right. 78:38.

questions.q: An-Naba' 78:38: «يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلرُّوحُ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: An-Naba' ends with someone wishing 'I were dust' (78:40). Why would anyone wish that?
questions.a: Out of regret on the Day of Judgement; the surah warns us now so that we never feel that regret.
